questions.question: What claim can a feature attribution support without additional causal evidence?
options: The model output depends on the feature under a declared explanation contract
Changing the feature in the real world will cause the predicted outcome to change
The feature is ethically acceptable to use
The training data contains no bias
questions.explanation: SHAP and LIME describe model behavior under reference, representation, and sampling assumptions. They do not prove real-world causality, fairness, or data quality.

questions.question: For an additive SHAP explanation, what should reconcile with the explained model output?
options: The base value plus all feature contributions
The largest feature contribution alone
The average feature value plus the model loss
The LIME kernel width plus the intercept
questions.explanation: Local accuracy or additivity means the base value plus the SHAP contributions reconstructs the model output on the scale being explained.

questions.question: Why can two valid SHAP explanations of the same prediction have different base values and contribution splits?
options: They may use different reference populations or feature-dependence assumptions
SHAP ignores the model prediction
The prediction must have changed
Feature names determine the base value
questions.explanation: An attribution is relative to a reference and a rule for handling unavailable features. Changing either changes the comparison question.

questions.question: Which measurement is essential before presenting a LIME explanation?
options: Weighted local fidelity between the surrogate and black-box outputs
Global training accuracy only
The number of production servers
The SHAP additivity residual only
questions.explanation: LIME explains through a local surrogate. If that surrogate does not reproduce black-box behavior in the weighted neighborhood, its coefficients are not useful evidence.

questions.question: What is a common attribution risk when features are strongly correlated?
options: Credit may swap, split, or be masked across related features
All methods become causal
The model stops producing predictions
Sampling variance becomes exactly zero
questions.explanation: Related features can substitute for one another under perturbation or coalition rules, so their individual rankings may be unstable or semantically misleading.

questions.question: A sampled explanation changes its top features across seeds while prediction quality remains stable. What should the release gate do?
options: Block or qualify the explanation until repeatability is understood
Publish the first run because the model prediction is stable
Average feature names alphabetically
Treat instability as proof of fairness
questions.explanation: Explanation outputs are separate production evidence. Stable predictions do not make unstable attribution rankings safe to present.

questions.question: Why should a team not average arbitrary LIME coefficients and label them global feature importance?
options: Each surrogate is fitted to a different local neighborhood and may use a different representation
LIME never produces coefficients
Global monitoring needs no sampling plan
Local models are always exact
questions.explanation: Local surrogate coefficients are conditional on each neighborhood and configuration. Global claims require a defined sampling and aggregation protocol.

questions.question: Which metadata belongs in a reproducible production explanation record?
options: Model, feature pipeline, explainer, reference data, parameters, seed, output scale, and policy versions
Only the displayed feature ranking
Only the end-user identifier
Only the model's training duration
questions.explanation: The explanation cannot be reproduced or audited unless every artifact and semantic choice that shaped it is versioned.
